profile.summary: scELMo uses large language models to describe genes (or other features and cell metadata) in text and to embed those descriptions, then combines the embeddings with single-cell expression data to make cell embeddings. Without training a new model the cell embeddings support clustering, batch effect correction and cell type annotation; a small fine-tuned adaptor handles harder tasks such as perturbation analysis.

summary_quotes.text: utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) as a generator for both the description of metadata information and the embeddings for such descriptions

We demonstrate that scELMo is capable of cell clustering, batch effect correction, and cell-type annotation without training a new model. Moreover, the fine-tuning framework of scELMo can help with more challenging task

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Feature information (for example genes or proteins) is turned into text, either from a database such as NCBI or as a summary written by an LLM, and the text is embedded with an LLM. A cell's embedding combines these feature embeddings with its expression profile. Unlike GenePT's arithmetic average, scELMo also offers a weighted average that uses expression levels as weights. In the fine-tuning framework, a light model (an adaptor) is trained on the gene embeddings and expression profiles.

quotes.text: we can either use prior knowledge from a known database such as NCBI or the summary given by LLMs as a prompt, and then generate the embeddings for the prompt based on LLM
we treated the gene expression levels as weights and computed the weighted average
GenePT utilized a naive arithmetic average
We then trained the model based on gene embeddings and expression profiles. Such model is also known as an adaptor

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: scELMo is a method, not a fixed checkpoint. Results depend on which LLM produced the descriptions and embeddings (the authors compared LLMs including GPT 3.5, GPT 4, Llama-2 70B and Mistral for hallucination) and on the averaging method. The authors host precomputed embeddings, including gene embeddings from gpt4-o and drug embeddings from GPT 3.5, on a website. A result should name the LLM, the embedding file and the averaging method.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Method that builds single-cell embeddings from LLM embeddings of text descriptions, with an optional fine-tuned adaptor.

quotes.text: we propose a method named scELMo (Single-cell Embedding from Language Models)

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: No pretrained network of its own. Zero-shot: averages of LLM feature embeddings weighted by expression (wa) or plain (aa). Fine-tuning: a small adaptor model trained on gene embeddings and expression.

quotes.text: we treated the gene expression levels as weights and computed the weighted average
Such model is also known as an adaptor

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A single-cell expression matrix and text descriptions of its features or cells, embedded by an LLM through the OpenAI API (or a DeepSeek alternative).

quotes.text: We rely on OpenAI API for query.
we provide an alternative solution based on [deepseekv2]

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Cell embeddings for clustering, batch correction and annotation; fine-tuned predictions for perturbation tasks.

quotes.text: scELMo is capable of cell clustering, batch effect correction, and cell-type annotation without training a new model

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not applicable for the zero-shot method, which trains nothing. The adaptor's size is not stated in the sources read.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: None for the zero-shot method. Descriptions come from NCBI and Ensembl gene names and from LLM summaries; datasets used are listed in the paper's Supplementary file 3.

quotes.text: we generated gene embeddings for gene names from both NCBI and Ensemble
All of the datasets and their download information are included in the Supplementary file 3.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: No numbered releases. Embedding sets differ by LLM (GPT 3.5, gpt4-o and others) and are hosted on the authors' website.

quotes.text: We have uploaded gene embeddings from gpt4-o and drug embeddings from GPT 3.5 in our website
https://sites.google.com/yale.edu/scelmolib

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no sequence model of its own; limits of the underlying LLMs are not stated.

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: Not stated. The precomputed embeddings are on a Google Sites page with no licence among the sources read.

facts.label: Code licence
facts.value: MIT, as stated in the paper's Codes and Datasets section ('The license is MIT license'); the repository has no LICENSE file and the README names no licence.

strengths.text: Zero-shot use needs no model training; the README says the demo runs on a normal computer within 10 minutes.

quotes.text: The demo tutorial can be finished in a normal computer within 10 minutes with a prepared environment.

strengths.text: Extends GenePT with expression-weighted averaging and with embeddings of other features and cell metadata.

quotes.text: Different from GenePT, we treated the gene expression levels as weights

strengths.text: The authors report that the fine-tuned adaptor is comparable to scGPT and Geneformer for annotation while needing fewer resources (authors' claim).

quotes.text: the fine-tuning results by combining the gene embeddings from GPT 3.5 or GenePT and our adaptor are comparable with FMs like scGPT

limitations.text: Generating new embeddings needs access to an LLM API (OpenAI, or DeepSeek as the alternative).

quotes.text: We rely on OpenAI API for query.

limitations.text: The MIT licence is stated only in the paper; the repository has no LICENSE file.

limitations.text: Results depend on the LLM chosen, and the authors screen LLMs for hallucinated descriptions.

quotes.text: A suitable LLM should not suffer from Hallucinations
that is, generating fake or incorrect information about our given feature information or cell information

limitations.text: No package; each task is a set of notebooks with its own dependencies, and perturbation analysis uses modified copies of CINEMA-OT, CPA and GEARS.

quotes.text: use the modifeid version provided in the **Perturbation Analysis** folder
